I have 13.1 mu of land. I keep 9 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu for cotton. That is the arrangement I have used for years, and I am not changing it.

For my winter wheat on those 9 mu, the crop is already in the ground. Last year I put down 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, and this year I did the same in October. Now it is early spring, so I will top-dress with 35 jin of urea per mu at green-up time. That is what I always do, and last year I got about 980 jin per mu. I will irrigate three times: once now at the recovery stage if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. My well can handle it. For spraying, I put herbicide on right after sowing, and I will do two more sprays — one for aphids and one for rust when I see it on my neighbor's field. I rotary-tilled before planting, same as every year. I use improved wheat seed, the kind I have been using for several years. The dealer keeps pushing new names, but my seed works and I save my own.

For summer maize on the same 9 mu, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. There is only about one week, so I use the no-till planter. I put 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, and that is usually enough. I use hybrid seed — Nongda or Denghai, about 2.5 jin per mu. I irrigate twice: once at the V6 stage if it does not rain, and once at tasseling. That is what I did last year and I got over 1100 jin per mu. I spray herbicide once before emergence and insecticide once when the borers show up. Some people add a plant growth regulator, and I usually do too, so that makes three sprays total.

For cotton on 4.1 mu, I start in late April. I plow the cotton field in spring and then rotary-till to break up the clods. I plant hybrid cotton seed, about 3 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I spread 60 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and I top-dress twice: once at flowering with urea, and once with some extra potash when the bolls are setting. Cotton needs more potassium, so I buy a bag of potassium chloride. I irrigate three times: at budding, flowering, and boll stage. The real cost is spraying — I spray 8 times this year for aphids, bollworm, and whitefly. Last year I only sprayed 6 times and I lost some bolls, so this year I am not cutting back. I expect about 520 jin of seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates.

I have to watch my wallet. Fertilizer prices are high again. My husband and son work in the city and send money home, but that does not mean I can waste it. Still, I would rather spend an extra 200 yuan on fertilizer than lose yield. A bad year means borrowing money. I watch what the other families in my village do — if Lao Wang and Auntie Liu are putting 50 jin of compound on their wheat, I do the same. I have been farming for 20 years, and I know that changing too much is how you get into trouble.
